newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mubarak blames Israel for spy suspect affair.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak blames Israel for spy suspect affair.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Friday Israeli leaders had squandered the chance to release an Israeli spy suspect through quiet diplomacy by making the affair public.
The Egyptian leader told Israel Television that the case of Israeli national Azam Azam was being handled by the courts and he could not interfere.
"You caused this affair," Mubarak said in an interview with the television's Arabic service, directing his remarks at Israel.

"Keep silent and conduct quiet contacts. Once you went public with the affair it was all over...I hold you responsible because you complicated the issue. Every day we hear a new declaration (from Israeli leaders) which causes the public to follow the issue and inquire about it," he said.

Azam, chief mechanic at an Israeli-owned textile factory in Egypt, was arrested last week by Egptian security authorities along with an Egyptian citizen. Egyptian newspapers said several charges, including espionage, were brought against the two men.
Israel has said Azam, 35, was innocent of any wrongdoing and has demanded his release.
"There is no basis to the charges attached to him. Azam is a private citizen innocent of any crime," Foreign Minister David Levy told parliament on Wednesday.
Mubarak said in an interview with the Israeli Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper this week that the Egyptian suspect admitted selling information to Azzam.
"The issue is now being handled by the courts and I can't interfere," Mubarak told Israel Television.
